questions.prompt: He ____ do his homework now because he won't have time later.
questions.explanation: “Has to” expresses necessity. The form “has” agrees with “he.”

questions.prompt: In Russia, I found some interesting stamps to ____ my collection.
questions.explanation: “Add to” means increase or make larger. The new stamps will increase the collection.

questions.prompt: He hopes the strong economy will ____ more new jobs.
questions.explanation: “Give rise to” means cause something to happen. A strong economy may create more jobs.

questions.prompt: The movie was, ____, one of the best films made this year.
questions.explanation: “In short” introduces a brief summary. The speaker summarizes a positive opinion of the movie.

questions.prompt: She made up her mind, ____, to quit her job and look for a new one.
questions.explanation: “Once and for all” means finally and decisively. She has made a firm decision.

questions.prompt: The company ____ a new way to market its clothes.
questions.explanation: “Hit upon” means suddenly thought of an idea. The company found a new marketing approach.

questions.prompt: He looks sad because he is ____ a divorce right now.
questions.explanation: “Going through” means experiencing a difficult or unpleasant situation.

questions.prompt: I want to find a job where I don't have to do exactly the same thing ____.
questions.explanation: “Day after day” means every day over a long period. The speaker wants work with more variety.

questions.prompt: She ____ staying in town during the vacation because she didn't have money to travel.
questions.explanation: “Resigned herself to” means accepted an unwanted situation she felt unable to change. It is followed here by “staying.”

questions.prompt: The lamp fell off the table ____. Nobody bumped it.
questions.explanation: “Of its own accord” means by itself, without an external action causing it to move.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Enough! I'm sick of asking you to stop! Can't you children behave ____?
lines.explanation: Mother wants the children to behave without having to be told.

lines.speaker: Jimmy
lines.text: I didn't do anything. She's bothering me!

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: ____ it’s the same thing! “He’s touching me!” “She’s bothering me!”
lines.explanation: The same complaints happen repeatedly every day.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Are you going to stop this arguing, or do I ____ stop the car?
lines.explanation: Mother asks whether stopping the car will be necessary.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: I want you to stop this nonsense, ____!
lines.explanation: Mother wants the arguing to stop completely and permanently.

lines.speaker: Jimmy
lines.text: Nancy better stop it before she makes me really mad.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: That's it! The two of you better ____ a quiet night at home. You're both grounded! No television! No toys! No friends! Nothing.
lines.explanation: Mother tells both children to accept the punishment. “Yourselves” refers to the two children.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: And no more talking or I will ____ your punishment.
lines.explanation: Mother warns that further talking will increase the punishment.

story.title: Idioms in context
paragraphs: My son is going through adolescence. With all that is going on in his life, he has a hard time remembering simple instructions. This gives rise to some problems.

For example, Wednesday is the day to wash clothes at our house. My son used to always leave money in his pockets. He never checked his clothes of his own accord. Day after day I reminded him to do it, but he always forgot. I resigned myself to the fact that I’d have to keep checking his pockets for him.

Then I hit upon an idea to put a stop to my son’s bad habit once and for all. I told my son, “I am going to put any money that I find in your pockets in a jar. When I have collected enough money, you have to use it to take me out to dinner and a movie.” In short, I wanted to teach my son a lesson in a positive way.

On the next Wednesday, I looked into my son’s room. He didn’t see me. I watched him sit down on his bed and check all of his pockets for money. He took a few coins out of his pants. I was so happy! However, to my surprise, my son put the coins back into the pocket. Then he stood up and got his wallet out of his bag. He took out a dollar bill and added it to the coins in the pocket on purpose! I never thought he wanted to take his mother to dinner and a movie. I was flattered!
